text.p: Tyndall Australia Ltd said on Thursday its subsidiary Tyndall Life Insurance Co Ltd has exchanged contracts for the purchase of all of the issued capital of Oceanic Capital Holdings Ltd.
The purchase price of A$40.516 will be satisfied in cash and through the provision of A$5 million of convertible notes maturing over the next three years and convertible at A$1.95.
A portion of the purchase consideration, including the convertible notes, is being withheld pending the satisfactory resolution of certain asset valuation issues, Tyndall said.
Completion of the deal, first announced on October 24, is expected on Friday.
"The acquisition of Oceanic bolsters the risk insurance operations of Tyndall and furthers its trans-Tasman financial services strategy," Tyndall said.
"This strategy concentrates on four main operational areas being risk insurance, funds management, superannuation administration and the provision of corporate and personal trustee services," it said
Following completion of the deal, Tyndall will have about A$6.45 billion in funds under management and administration. Tyndall is 51 percent owned by Guinness Peat Group Plc.

Oceanic, which is involved in funds management and insurance in Australia and New Zealand, is owned by Financial Insurance Fund L.P., a U.S.-based group of investors and insurers. It was previously owned by the State Bank of South Australia.
